teaser.text: Lumentum Holdings Inc. sells the lasers and optical hardware that move information through fiber networks, while also selling lasers that help machines make things and sensors see. Its business is easiest to understand by following a product from the light it creates to the customer who buys it, and then following the dollar back through factories, suppliers and investment.

stock.meta_description: Lumentum stock forecast with scenario prices, cash generation, valuation, and the business drivers behind each case.
stock.opening: Lumentum’s weighted value is $728.31 in October 2027, a 13% loss. It hinges on continued earnings growth, profitable production ramps and cash conversion as the valuation multiple compresses.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Lumentum’s business, rivals, management and risks shape the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could Lumentum’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: Weighted value is $728.31 in October 2027, a 13% loss. It is $813.14 in October 2029, a 2% loss, with dividends included. The forecast assigns 30% probability to bear and 50% to base. Bull has 20% probability.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Lumentum?

paragraphs.text: The base case assumes AI demand continues, 1.6T products and optical switches add volume, and Greensboro begins contributing after qualification. Investment and working capital limit cash conversion, while valuation compression offsets much of the earnings growth. The shares move from $791.07 to $900.59. The 50% probability reflects the balance between strong guidance and execution risks.

The bear row falls to $2,014M and then $1,410M before recovering to $1,581M, reflecting an inventory correction and lower utilization. The bull row reaches $2,646M and then $3,440M before ending at $4,085M, requiring sustained AI demand, 1.6T and switch adoption, and better yields. Recent estimate beats and the R300’s more-than-$100M quarterly run rate support the upside, but the historical EBITDA fall to $95.1M shows why the bear remains credible.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Lumentum really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation adds a second reading. It does not appear as another cash payment in the cash-flow statement, but it compensates employees with ownership. Subtracting it from free cash flow therefore produces a more demanding measure of the cash return available to existing shareholders. On that basis, the latest recovery looks much less generous, and the five-year cumulative picture is weaker still.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Lumentum today?

paragraphs.text: Lumentum’s price assumes that strong optical demand will become sustained profit and cash flow. Its equity value is $77,796.4 million, while enterprise value—the value of the operating business after accounting for debt and cash—is $76,695.4 million. Yet investors are paying 25.4 times trailing revenue, before the company pays its workers, factories, and suppliers.

blocks.heading: What has Lumentum guided for the next quarter?

paragraphs.text: Management’s August 11, 2026 guidance calls for September-quarter revenue of $1,225 million to $1,275 million. It calls for a 39.5%–40.5% non-GAAP operating margin. Diluted EPS is $4.05–$4.35. The guidance is based on 102.0 million diluted shares, and its revenue midpoint is above the $1.25 billion quarterly milestone.

blocks.heading: Has Lumentum kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: There is tangible delivery to credit. A prior forecast of more than $600 million for the June quarter was followed by actual revenue of $1,006.3 million. Management also said shipments of 1.6-terabit transceivers had begun as planned. A transceiver sends and receives data by converting electrical signals into light and back again; the 1.6T example combines eight 200-gigabit-per-second lanes. Capacity matters because demand helps shareholders only if Lumentum can build reliable modules on time.

Revenue rose in every quarter shown across the eight-quarter sequence. That matters more than one record quarter because it shows acceleration rather than a single shipment spike. Components and Systems both contributed, so the improvement was broader than one product launch.

Profit followed shipments. Gross margin improved sharply from the prior-year quarter, and operating income moved from a loss to a substantial profit. Management reported record 800G transceiver shipments and the start of 1.6T production, alongside better manufacturing yield and utilization. The current earnings base therefore rests mainly on products already shipping at scale, while the faster generation is still entering production.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Lumentum's next results?

paragraphs.text: Lumentum is scheduled to report the September quarter on November 5, 2026. Revenue will show whether the accelerated target arrived, while operating margin will show whether manufacturing economics kept pace. Cash flow and capital spending will reveal how much of that progress can finance the following quarter.
